title: Session-Cohesive Geo-Gateway Steering with Circuit Breakers and Load Shedding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a session-cohesive, geo-aware gateway steering layer for the hosted API that supports active-active request serving while preserving streaming/session continuity, bounded tail latency SLOs, and graceful degradation under cross-region overloads.
acceptance_criteria: New gateway steering supports per-session affinity tokens and resume tokens for HTTP/2 streaming and server-sent events (SSE) so resuming a streaming session in a secondary region recovers within one second for >=95% of synthetic resume attempts.
End-to-end 99th percentile request latency across regions does not regress by more than 15ms under normal load when steering is enabled compared to baseline.
Circuit breaker opens and routes traffic to fallback pools when a region breaches error-rate SLO (>1.5% 5m error rate) for 30s, with automatic cooling/gradual rejoin.
Load shedding policy discards or downgrades non-critical requests (bulk embeddings, low-priority batch jobs) before user-facing generation requests when capacity pressure >85% for >60s.
End-to-end test harness demonstrates session continuity for long-lived streams across an orchestrated region failover with zero token loss (or clear token semantics) in >=90% of runs.
All changes feature tracing headers and metrics that feed into Redwood Console dashboards and alerting (SLO burn rate, per-region active sessions, shed-rate).
design_decisions: Use a two-layer steering: deterministic hash-based primary selection (geo + customer tier) and a dynamic policy layer that can override for health/capacity reasons.
Session affinity implemented via stable session-token with embedded origin-region + monotonic resume-counter; tokens are opaque to clients but verifiable by gateways.

Streaming resume uses a resumable append-only sequence model: each gateway persists minimal resume state (last-acknowledged token index) to a durable, low-latency cross-region store (read-replica friendly) and issues a short-lived resume nonce for security.

Circuit breaker per-region, per-customer tier with samples taken at the ingress gateway: error-rate, latency-p90/p99, queue-depth; tripping thresholds are conservative and include adaptive cooldown with exponential backoff.

Load shedding operates by request-class priority: realtime generation > chat message streaming > reranking > batch embeddings. Lower classes receive 503 with Retry-After or are downgraded to queued post-processing when capacity constrained.
KV/prefix cache invalidation remains local to region; cross-region fallbacks accept eventual cold-start cost — we instrument to quantify token-cost impact.
Traffic mirroring for validation: subset of sessions mirrored to candidate fallback region to validate behavioral parity without affecting user-visible latency.
Security: resume tokens are HMAC-signed with region-specific keys stored in KMS; gateway validates signature before accepting resume.
Avoid sticky heavy-weight TCP affinity; prefer application-level resume tokens to keep LB layer stateless and compatible with autoscaling.
implementation_steps: 1) Extend gateway API to accept and emit Session-Token and Resume-Nonce headers (RFC-style names: X-Session-Token, X-Resume-Nonce).
2) Implement lightweight resume-state store shim and deploy a read-optimized cross-region replica (initial PoC in us-east/us-west).
3) Add steering policy service hooks: health/capacity signals ingestion and decision API (evaluate(session_token, request_meta) -> target_region|fallback).
4) Implement circuit breaker module at gateway edge that watches rolling windows and publishes events to control plane for visibility and manual overrides.
5) Implement request-class tagging at ingress and prioritized token bucket queues per class to enable graceful shedding.
6) Add streaming resume logic to runtime: emit checkpoints for sequence index and accept resume requests that reconcile last-acknowledged index.
7) End-to-end integration tests (see testing_plan) and gradual canary rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
8) Instrumentation and dashboards: SLO burn, shed-rate, resume-success-rate, per-region active-streams, circuit-breaker state timeline.
9) Documentation and SDK updates: document headers, error semantics (503/429/421 for resume failures), client guidance for resume retries and backoff.
10) Post-mortem/ops playbook creation for region failover scenarios including manual promotion, key rotation impact on resume tokens, and cache-warm strategies.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token generation/validation and resume HMAC verification.
Integration tests for steering decisions under simulated health signals using the test harness (cross-region latency, partial regional outage).
Chaos tests: kill region compute, inject 5xx spikes, and verify circuit breaker opens and traffic moves according to policy.
Synthetic streaming continuity tests: create 10k concurrent streams, simulate region failover, assert resume-success-rate and token loss metrics.
Performance benchmarks: measure p50/p95/p99 baseline with steering disabled and enabled at 10%, 50% steering traffic to ensure acceptable overhead.
Customer-facing beta with two internal Redwood customers to validate real-world session patterns and gather UX feedback on resume behaviors.
monitoring_and_slos: Primary SLOs: request availability 99.95% per region; streaming resume success-rate 99% for resumed streams within 2s; request p99 latency budget 300ms for short requests.
Derived metrics: per-region error-rate 5m, circuit-breaker open-count, shed-rate per request-class, resume-latency histogram, cross-region cold-start token-cost estimation.
Alerts: SLO burn-rate > 3 for 10min (pagable), circuit breaker blackout (>2 regions simultaneously with breakers open) -> immediate page, shed-rate >5% for high-priority class -> ops review.
Tracing: propagate trace-id and session-token; ensure spans include steering decision and final target region to troubleshoot misroutes.
Dashboards: per-customer and per-tier steering heatmap, resume success funnel, aggregated cost delta when fallback used.
rollout_plan: Canary on internal infra: deploy steering library in frontends and enable for 0.5% of traffic with full observability.
Enable steering for internal dev accounts (5%), gather resume metrics and issue fixes.
Customer beta opt-in (10% of customers), prepare support-runbook and rapid rollback hooks.
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% for non-critical regions over two weeks with automated rollback if p99 regresses >20% or resume-success <90%.
Finalize GA when monitoring shows stable SLOs and shed-rate under 0.5% for high-priority classes.
rollback_plan: Immediate toggle to disable steering policy and return to deterministic primary region routing via feature flag.
If circuit-breaker misfires due to bad config: revert to previous thresholds and clear breaker state with coordinated cache/metric reset.
Revoke region-specific resume-key and reissue global key if resume-token verification bug discovered; provide client communication timeline.
Fallback to manual traffic-drain procedure described in ops playbook when automated rollback insufficient.
